Case05 uses cells for computation, connected patches for spatial interpretation,
and plate-carried patch networks for history. These are derived **results**, not
new biological processes. Case05's six active process interfaces remain Environmental
filtering, Dispersal, Biotic filtering, Evolution, Speciation, and Extinction.

The completed v8 Case05 source contains 200 extant selected plants, 66 native
time slices from 325 to 0 Ma, five ancestral-response draws, and four explicit
dispersal schemes. Its geographic field is a *location-density distribution*
per active lineage. It is not cell occupancy or historical species richness.

## Six result functions

| Function | Input | Output | Important boundary |
|---|---|---|---|
| `hee_result_patches()` | Time-matched environmental support, land area, terrestrial adjacency | Connected supported patches | Support is not occupancy. |
| `hee_result_patch_links()` | Patch memberships and plate-carriage cell transfer | Directed patch links, including splits/mergers | Carriage is not dispersal. |
| `hee_result_patch_stability()` | Patches and temporal links | Patch-history networks and link-wise environmental changes | Network-wide SD includes simultaneous spatial heterogeneity. |
| `hee_result_refugia_candidates()` | Patches, links, supported-area contractions | Candidate ecological refugia | Not confirmed persistence; location mass remains separate. |
| `hee_result_corridor_flow()` | Joint posterior movement mass on active cell-to-cell edges | Patch-level movement flow | Cannot infer from marginal location maps. |
| `hee_result_donor_recipient()` | Patch-level joint movement flow | Exporter, recipient, exchange-hub labels | Not demographic source/sink. |

The first four operate on the saved v8 data. The last two are implemented and
tested, but their **Case05 empirical results remain uncomputed** because v8
saved location marginals and transition diagnostics, not joint posterior
source-to-target movement mass. Neither a least-cost line nor the product of
two location marginals is substituted for this missing object.

This is a limitation of the **saved output**, not a proof that edge posteriors
are impossible. The pruning code already computes forward and backward branch
messages. A rerun can reconstruct the transition operators and stream joint
edge posteriors. It must retain the latent post-diffusion, pre-carriage state:
the current composed transition is plate carriage multiplied by diffusion, so
endpoint coordinate changes alone cannot distinguish movement from plate
motion. A separate time-ordered least-cost graph could show *potential*
corridors now, but those routes are not posterior use of a corridor.

The v8 geographic state represents one lineage location at a time, rather
than a population count or a complete occupied geographic range. Even after
edge posteriors are available, the resulting exporter/recipient labels describe
modelled lineage-location transitions, not numbers of dispersing seeds or
demographic source/sink populations.

## Case05 computation

The reproducible runner is
`scripts/case05_v8_patch_history_results.R`. It uses the installed
`HmscEcoEvo` functions, the saved HMSC ancestral beta draws, the native
PALEOMAP carrier tracks, and the four v8 location-density fields. The 4-degree
grid preserves its original land mask; ocean has no value in PNG or GeoTIFF.

For each active lineage and time, the script applies the time-matched ancestral
response to the same environmental axes used by the fitted modern HMSC. The
probit transform is called an *environmental support index* because the modern
prevalence intercept and observation process are deliberately not interpreted
as an ancestral ecological niche. At each time, supported land is identified
with an explicitly chosen 0.6 index threshold. The threshold is a scenario
choice, not a fitted survival probability.

Three representative extant tips are followed along their unique ancestral
paths: `Ilex_aquifolium`, `Camellia_sinensis`, and
`Jasminum_officinale`. Each time slice is partitioned into connected supported
patches. The original 1-degree carrier `track_id` correspondence determines
how their 4-degree patches overlap between successive palaeogeographies; this
can yield one-to-many splits and many-to-one mergers. A link does not prove a
population persisted through the interval.

The full set of active lineages is used for environmental-opportunity maps and
tables, while patch histories and refugia candidates are explicitly limited
to these three illustrated tip-to-root paths. The analysis does not silently
extrapolate the focal patch results to all 200 species.

An environmental-opportunity contraction is recorded when supported land area
on one focal ancestral path drops by at least 10% between native 5-Myr slices.
A contraction-surviving patch must be at least 100,000 km2, have incoming
carriage from a supported older patch, and retain another carriage link into
the next slice. The package returns an explicitly named *candidate ecological
refugium*. A second 25% contraction cutoff is saved as a sensitivity check.
The four dispersal schemes are compared by integrating each lineage's separate
location density over supported cells; this does not multiply geography by
environment or turn the result into occupancy.

For extrapolation, a cell is flagged when any of the eight historical input
axes falls outside the 1st-99th percentile range of the corresponding modern
HMSC training data. This is a separate diagnostic, never a penalty on
biological probability. Because the eight-axis envelope is a simple marginal
range screen, it does not establish full multivariate analog status.

## Reading the outputs

The result folder is
`outputs/HmscEcoEvo/case05_v8_four_scheme_comparison_20260926/08_patch_history_results`
under the project root. `all_active_lineages_environmental_opportunity.csv`
contains the full 200-tip, 66-time opportunity audit; the number of active
ancestral branches naturally changes with time. `*_patch_cells.csv` and
`*_patches.csv` give exact spatial memberships and summaries. The
`*_plate_carried_patch_links.csv` files retain split and merger structure.
`*_link_environmental_changes.csv` separates change along a link from
variation among simultaneous patches. `*_candidate_refugia.csv` identifies
contraction-surviving candidates with an independent location-mass evidence
column. `not_computed_evidence_gates.csv` records the unavailable outputs.

The `maps/` folder contains PNG for viewing and GeoTIFF for numerical reuse.
All corresponding panels use the same 0-1 support-index scale or the same
declared categorical evidence classes. The sea is NA, not zero.

## Why these distinctions matter

Keppel et al. define refugia through environment, space and time, including
retreat, persistence and possible later expansion. Gavin et al. argue that
fossils, distribution models and phylogeography provide complementary evidence.
Accordingly, Case05's present outputs are *candidates*, not validated ancient
populations. Martensen et al. show why connectivity must be considered across
dynamic habitat patches; the package's carriage links are only the geographic
continuity substrate, not their full reachable-habitat metric. TARDIS uses
time-ordered landscape graphs for possible deep-time routes; the Case05 v8
output does not yet contain joint posterior route use. McRae et al.'s circuit
current is likewise not silently renamed posterior flow. Pulliam's source/sink
classification requires reproduction and mortality, which the present
phylogeographic case does not estimate.
